court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Smt. Radhika W/O. Anup Gupta vs Anup S/O. Sharadkumar Gupta

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Anup S/O. Sharadkumar Gupta (husband) and Radhika Anup Gupta (wife)
parties.respondent_defendant: Radhika Anup Gupta (wife) and Anup S/O. Sharadkumar Gupta (husband)

facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife filed an application under Section 24 of the Act seeking maintenance pendente lite. The Family Court allowed the application and granted Rs.25,000/- per month to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The quantum of maintenance should be commensurate to the standard of living and status of the parties.
legal_principles.held: This Court had earlier remanded the matter for deciding the application for grant of maintenance pendente lite afresh by observing that the quantum of maintenance should be commensurate to the standard of living and status of the parties.
cited_cases: Smt. Radhika W/O. Anup Gupta vs Anup S/O. Sharadkumar Gupta, (2026) X SCC Y
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for determining the amount of maintenance

legal_principles.principle: The wife is entitled to a life with the same standard of living as that of her husband.
legal_principles.held: She submitted that the wife is entitled for a life with the same standard of living as that of her husband and considering the solid financial position of the husband, grant of amount of Rs.25,000/- per month towards maintenance pendente lite is very meagre.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for determining the wife's maintenance rights

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order granting maintenance pendente lite to the wife was set aside.

use_for_drafting: assisting with maintenance and alimony disputes
